constraints.statement: A member-owned row declares no context: its owning member supplies source context, and a bounded context holds it only by its own import. Meaning follows the occurrence's owning clause, with qualification or stated predicate; equal spelling establishes no equivalence. In particular, semantic equivalence of realisations differs from §5 Semantic Equivalence of concepts. Importing or relating clauses are not second owners. Index conservation requires every predecessor row retained with unchanged bounded-context identity and locus moved to its successor owner, with owner moves recorded per row; routes supply provenance only.

grounding.quote:
The engine should carry identity safely. The domain should define
semantic identity law for its own constitutional objects (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Identity is scoped, typed, unique and stable enough for its governed purpose, made unique through hierarchy and type rather than a flat global string convention. One string format cannot define identity across all products/runtime surfaces. Readability is secondary to uniqueness and stable governed meaning. The engine should carry identity safely; the domain should define its constitutional objects' semantic identity law.

grounding.quote:
Identity is always scoped. At minimum, identity should be interpretable
through authority, kind and value.

constraints.statement: Identity is always scoped and should be interpretable at minimum through authority, kind and value. These are semantic coordinates, not a prescribed string concatenation or mandatory visible serialisation.

grounding.quote:
- no two live objects of the same kind may share the same identity within
  the same authority scope;
- aliasing across scopes remains explicit; and
- serialisation preserves enough hierarchy to prevent accidental
  collision.

constraints.statement: No two live objects of the same kind may share identity within the same authority scope. Cross-scope aliasing remains explicit; serialisation preserves sufficient hierarchy to prevent accidental collisions. Global uniqueness of naked strings is not required.

grounding.quote:
Identity is typed. Different kinds of thing should not be collapsed into
one undifferentiated identity space.

constraints.statement: Identity is typed; different kinds should not collapse into one identity space. Example kinds are goal, intent, requirement, requirement_family, acceptance_criterion, scenario, design_decision, published_function, carrier_surface, release, install, run, function_call, continuation and event. A family identity is not treated as a concrete requirement identity; release version is not treated as object identity.

exceptions: Stability does not mean every identity is immutable forever.

grounding.quote: Identity should remain stable for the governed lifecycle it serves.

constraints.statement: Identity should stay stable enough over its governed lifecycle to support traceability, comparison, replay, publication and supersession. If identity changes, the method should explicitly relate old and new rather than silently reuse the old identity for a different object.

grounding.quote:
A boundary claim names its
object, the evidence that supports it and the basis it holds on, and it
holds only as far as that evidence goes (P3, P6).

constraints.statement: Storage, schema and name do not establish a boundary. A boundary claim names its object, evidence and basis and holds only as far as the evidence goes; beyond evidence is undecided. Task-bounded material sufficiency under RF-003 is not completeness and does not establish screening of the interior from everything outside. The stronger statistical Markov boundary remains a hypothesis on which no work relies as established; a profile using it states epistemic status. Generic boundary law is available without adopting optional WORLD_MODEL, whose §4 refines it.
constraints.uncertainty: RF-003, hypothesis law and the WORLD_MODEL refinement are not supplied.

grounding.quote:
- no reader should infer that a readable identity is safer or more
  authoritative than an opaque one merely because it looks meaningful.

constraints.statement: Readability is recognition convenience; uniqueness and scoped meaning govern. A GUID may be lawful without human meaning. A readable identity is lawful only while preserving scoped uniqueness. No reader should infer greater safety or authority merely from meaningful appearance.

conditions: Hierarchy is appropriate to the identity.
exceptions: Not every serialisation needs all four visible segments.

grounding.quote: Identity should be made unique by hierarchy where appropriate.

constraints.statement: Identity should be made unique by hierarchy where appropriate; authority / kind / value / revision is a useful model whose semantics should be available. The examples distinguish product requirement REQ-F-CAPABILITY-001, product requirement_family REQ-F-CAPABILITY, runtime run UUID and release-authority release 1.0.0-rc.1. Family/member and runtime run/domain requirement remain distinct kinds even when serialised as strings.

grounding.quote:
Those rules should optimise for uniqueness, replay
safety and event-stream integrity.

The domain defines which identity kinds exist, how they
are distinguished, what makes them unique, and how they are parsed or
read.

constraints.statement: Runtime generation rules should optimise uniqueness, replay safety and event-stream integrity; the engine should not impose domain-specific grammar on domain-owned objects. The domain defines its kinds, distinctions, uniqueness and parsing/reading. Runtime transport does not license silently inventing domain meaning.

grounding.quote: composition, delegation and projection restrict it or carry it faithfully and never widen it.
Recording a ruling cannot widen it.

constraints.statement: Authority's owner, kind, subject, scope and basis survive every carrier; composition, delegation and projection restrict or faithfully carry authority, never widen it. Capability, labels, reachability, actor identity and payload shape create none. Elevation, transfer, split, merge, proxy grant, revocation and retirement require an explicit authority decision with identifiable basis; a step-produced decision cannot be re-acquired as if pre-existing. Proxy grants name grantor, actor, subject, scope, permitted/excluded decisions, validity, delegation rights, revocation and provenance. Direct/proxied decisions preserve source, subject and basis, acting identity and mode, scope, change class, disposition and supersession. Recording cannot widen a ruling. Proxy identity remains distinct from human-authority identity; proxy authority makes neither implementer self-review independent nor unrelated runtime/domain authority available.
constraints.uncertainty: FOUNDATIONS owns the full no-authority and proxy-prohibition lists; only supplied instances are asserted here.

conditions: A derived domain overrides runtime identity defaults for its own kinds.
constraints.statement: An override is lawful only if it preserves scoped uniqueness, explicit kind distinction, deterministic parsing or reading, family/member non-aliasing and stable downstream traceability. It is published in domain authority and cannot exist only as ad hoc hidden regex assumptions. The bound realisation's default publication surfaces are governed outside this member by DESIGN_MODULE §12.
constraints.uncertainty: The external runtime-publication law is not supplied.

conditions: A domain overrides defaults published by its bound runtime realisation.

grounding.quote:
The important rule is that identity overrides are visible in domain
authority, auditable, and recoverable without reverse-engineering regexes
from implementation code (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Publish the override in a lawful domain-authority surface, visible, auditable and recoverable without reverse-engineering implementation regexes. At minimum the domain should publish kinds in scope, serialisation/readable forms, uniqueness scope/hierarchy, and distinctions between grouping and concrete executable/traceable identities.

exceptions: Family markers, display aliases or prose headings may be first-class identities only when governing identity law says they are identities of their own kind.

grounding.quote:
Regex extraction from prose is not a complete identity model. At most,
regex may be a provisional extractor over a surface whose identity law is
already defined elsewhere

constraints.statement: Regex over prose is at most a provisional extractor over already-defined identity law, never a complete identity model. Parsers distinguish concrete kinds from grouping labels; family markers, aliases and headings are not promoted to executable/traceable identities absent their own first-class kind under law. Acceptance criteria, test cases and similar subordinate identities do not collapse into requirement identity merely because their forms derive from requirement tokens. A domain needing families should publish requirement_family identities explicitly.

grounding.quote: These may relate, but they are not interchangeable (P3, P6).
by P6 none grants the other's authority

constraints.statement: Object identity, release identity, publication/revision coordinates and mutable discovery selectors may relate but are not interchangeable and confer none of each other's authority. Release version is a release-process fact, not the live constitutional identity of every project object.
constraints.uncertainty: The highest-published selector replacement is separately marked proposed and pending acceptance in the supplied provenance section.

conditions: An identity surface is being defined or audited.

grounding.quote:
If those questions cannot be answered, the identity surface is
under-defined (P3).

constraints.statement: Ask who owns the identity; its denoted kind; its uniqueness scope; lifecycle stability; whether readability is over-trusted; whether parsing distinguishes families, members, aliases and revisions unambiguously; and whether it is runtime, domain-semantic or release identity. If these cannot be answered, the surface is under-defined.

grounding.quote:
Implementations should prefer typed identity readers, explicit
identity-kind distinctions, and source-of-authority parsing contracts.

constraints.statement: Implementations should prefer typed readers, explicit kind distinctions and authority-based parsing contracts, and should avoid regex mining as the identity model, silent family/concrete coercion and engine grammar leaking into domain semantics. Where a project relies on those patterns, the first lawful repair contains the immediate bug; enduring repair publishes explicit identity law and moves implementations onto it. This is member policy applied under project design authority.

grounding.quote:
the actor, the
executor, the domain operation and the functor kind are different
coordinates

constraints.statement: ODD graph traversal and F_D/F_P/F_H are not a_c traversal records or functor kinds by spelling. Executive, Worker and Reviewer are relations over steps; role names confer no operation. Actor, executor, domain operation and functor kind remain different coordinates. Referencing externally owned traversal/functor definitions and core results does not transfer their ownership.

conditions: A product is represented as built using ODD.

grounding.quote:
A product
whose constructive carrier stays hidden in imperative loops, local service
logic or product-specific orchestration scripts is not yet built with this
profile (P0, P6).

constraints.statement: Build a GTL/ABG domain product with typed assets/nodes and named published graph functions bound into a GTL module. ABG owns traversal governance, runtime facts, provenance, continuation and re-entry after each publish boundary. Commands/services are cooperative bounded-step subsystems publishing assets/evidence and returning control. Visible current state projects constructive history. A hidden imperative constructive carrier leaves the product not yet built with this profile. The graph is the process model; automation must not outrun a lawful manual traversal. Consumers bind conforming roles in their Product, requirements, design and immutable dependency identity; implementations may prove or falsify conformance but supply no method authority.

grounding.quote:
Where a product is both ODD and
world-model-driven, this profile governs graph-native structure and ODD
product shape and the world-model profile governs world-model semantics,
publication and composition law. The two compose (P1, P4a).

To build one concrete product correctly it must then read the
product-specific method and the local authority surfaces (P1, P2).

constraints.statement: SPEC_METHOD supplies the general constitutional chain and lawful re-entry. ODD supplies graph-native traversal governance and product-authoring structure; it does not replace domain semantic methods or local ratified intent, product definition, requirements and design. A world-model product additionally takes semantics, publication and composition law from WORLD_MODEL. Software-development local lines include GTL surfaces. Reading ODD alone can convey the paradigm but does not suffice for domain-correct construction; the constructing actor must read its product-specific method and local authority surfaces.
constraints.uncertainty: External constitutional/domain laws and concrete Product authority surfaces are not supplied.

exceptions: A project-local distribution copy is optional and is not the default.

grounding.quote:
The selected immutable RC is consumer authority. Installed bytes must
match that cut;

constraints.statement: Consumers select one complete immutable release. Mutable source authors a future cut and governs no consumer before publication and explicit selection. Product definitions address installed distributions by exact logical release URI and installed-manifest digest independent of local path. Installed bytes must match the selected cut; mutable source and moving selectors cannot silently repair, replace or outrank it. Mismatch is an adoption defect repaired by selecting/installing one complete released cut, never mixing members; selected release wins over a disagreeing installation. Only method members are constitutional; tier-3 profiles are method surfaces when selected.
constraints.uncertainty: README's member enumeration and external installation law are not supplied.

conditions: One declared vector or edge traversal of a published graph is the probabilistic work unit.

grounding.quote:
The vector declares the admissible external traversal space: required
upstream assets; target asset or output contract; required context; role
or capability expectation; governing evaluators and gates; provenance
obligation; and the lawful stop, hold, gap, continuation or completion
states.

constraints.statement: Each vector declares required upstream assets, target/output contract, context, role/capability expectation, evaluators/gates, provenance and lawful stop/hold/gap/continuation/completion states. Context fits the actor's envelope; the actor retains its internal path. The profile governs contract, evidence, provenance and control truth without making the framework executor of domain-internal strategy. F_H invokes explicit adjudication only under declared authority/ambiguity policy and grants no ambient traversal, semantic or closure authority.

conditions: A graph function refines one published outer vector into a declared inner workflow.

grounding.quote:
the inner steps conserve it and every applicable
invariant; and each inner function's input satisfies its declared domain
and preconditions, as AC-016 requires.

constraints.statement: The outer vector stays the callable constitutional contract; inner steps preserve it and every applicable invariant, and inputs satisfy declared domains/preconditions. ODD §11.8 cumulative carried environment is the specialised contract, conserved as profile law rather than generalised into core. Retained functions should declare environment.requires, environment.provides and environment.carries. A later function's domain is environment.requires, which may require any typed binding in the cumulative environment, not only the immediately previous output. Changes to ACTIVATION §4, §11.8, outer vector or function environment declaration invalidate the binding until reevaluation.
constraints.uncertainty: Full §11.8 and AC-016 clauses are not supplied.

conditions: The Product adopts ODD.

grounding.quote: no operative step, callable surface or capability stays only in prose, prompt memory, an orchestration loop or a service method

constraints.statement: Every operative constructive step has a named typed published reacquirable carrier; callers bind the published outer carrier, never hidden inner vectors. Inner boundaries are published and governed by the loop as outer boundaries are. GraphFunction and GTL module are profile carrier/publication choices; a machine-readable catalogue's retained functions should expose at minimum name, inputs, outputs, intent and public/helper role. Outcome traversal precedes declarative carrier, which precedes minimal adapter code. Imperative code transports/persists facts but cannot privately decide domain meaning, semantic target movement, step selection, closure, lineage or constructive workflow truth. A product supplying this framework builds its framework behaviour through graph functions. Actor acquisition precedes carrier/loop declaration and code: general method, domain method where one exists, local authority surfaces.
constraints.uncertainty: The referenced detailed fourteen-step invocation sequence and two reading orders are not supplied; the source qualifies effects of skipping the order with usually.

conditions: The Product adopts ODD.

grounding.quote: each traversal has exactly one execution authority

constraints.statement: Exactly one execution authority per traversal owns selection/advance, actor invocation/supervision, retry, continuation/re-entry, runtime events and closure fold. Workers, product code, plugins, services and queries return evidence/policy input/control and own none of these; two independently claiming controllers leave the product not ODD-correct. A worker cannot close an edge, emit runtime events, mutate ledgers or decide re-entry: output is candidate until evaluated and report is observation. Neither artifact, worker report, process success nor liveness alone closes an edge. Closure folds admitted evidence; workspace counts only through ledger, and evaluators attend only admitted ledger rows reachable by declared lineage. Direct append or side-ledger mutation outside ABG is forbidden.
constraints.uncertainty: The five-surface execution-authority audit, triggering changes and full closure-prevention conditions are referenced but not enumerated.

conditions: The Product adopts ODD.

grounding.quote: a correction keeps the identity of what it corrects, so it appends or supersedes and never rewrites

constraints.statement: Model synthesis, gap discovery, next-action selection and action evaluation retain separate authorities, expressed as synthesize_model, eval_gap, evaluate_next and evaluate_action; a design, ticket, module or proof names which it implements/consumes. Reports, queries, services and summaries do not become rival traversal truth. Visible projections reconcile admitted truth or fail closed. Every closure-relevant callout is admitted to immutable ledger/event log; corrections append/supersede, never rewrite. Every closure decision and next-action selection is reproducible by replay from carriers referencing causal predecessors. Lawful but undecided work yields without failure classification, retaining the same edge and replay-visible resume basis; yield differs from retry, block and timeout.
constraints.uncertainty: Ledger fields, full replay inputs, predecessor-chain details and post_yield_resume contract are outside the supplied sections.

conditions: The Product adopts ODD.

grounding.quote: selection data decides no predicate, so it maps to no core value

constraints.statement: Selected outcome bounds the loop: before invocation every action binds current gap to exact targets/obligations, and ranking considers only published lawful actions. Once a terminal condition holds, no further material work is selected without another admitted basis. Reprice requests constitutional re-entry and selects nothing. Edge closure is evidence toward Product acceptance, not acceptance. Closure decisions form a closed sum type; evaluate_next is total. Each closure decision/audit outcome maps to exactly one core value for its named predicate, with deciding cause included. Edge-predicate closure and acceptance-predicate disposition do not count toward each other. Selection data maps to no core value; typed no-action decides inability to select a published lawful action and maps by its cause, while preceding closure retains its own edge value. Product owns priority policy; profile supplies graph-following default and decision/no-action types.
constraints.uncertainty: Detailed closure mappings, two no-action causes, terminal conditions and reprice continuation contracts are not supplied.

conditions: The Product adopts ODD.

grounding.quote: one failing or unestablished clause leaves the product not built correctly

constraints.statement: Every automated move must be available to an actor holding only declared surfaces; agentic artifacts take effect only by admission against deterministic criteria, and conformance evidence does not ratify law. Negative boundary proof exercises the supported authority path with the real authority-bearing input invalidated and shows refusal before prohibited effect; manufactured refusal, blocked event, gap or verdict proves nothing about that path. Absence in source, package, installation and runtime are distinct claims. Where an installable development form exists, decisive proof runs against it; isolated environment/proving lane are should-level choices. Refined inner chains close outer carriers only after fold-back preserves outer contract and zoomed/unzoomed views agree. A live requirement without a witness is a gap keeping the carrier open until realised, deferred or repriced out by its owner. Scenario bundles should clarify boundary, assets, vectors, paths and closing evidence. Every §11 clause must hold for correct construction; a failing or unestablished clause leaves correctness unestablished, without equating those states.
constraints.uncertainty: Full core clauses, concrete negative-proof mechanism, proof witnesses and scenario requirements are not supplied; no Product is assessed here.

grounding.quote:
The installed product must not assume prior knowledge of the target project's
domain (P6, P3).

constraints.statement: Installed builder must not assume target-domain knowledge. A clean install is described as installing the ODD product, authoring target intent/product definition/requirements/realisation root, then traversing the graph for target outputs. Target owns one stdo_<label>.json per distinct Product WHAT locating constitutional, local/collective reference-frame basis, realisation, work and composition surfaces; constitutional surfaces under SPEC_METHOD; one or more realisation roots bound by how.build_tenants; and its outputs/evidence, including design/code/tests/documents/proof in software development and appropriately named artifacts in other domains.

conditions: A released installed product helps build its next version.

grounding.quote:
Self-hosting is lawful only while the installed product in use stays
distinct from the product under development.

constraints.statement: Self-hosting is lawful only while released installed builder and product under development remain distinct, never one mixed authority surface. Framework preserves distinct territories, authority surfaces, runtime state and project-owned specification/build-tenant surfaces. Silent merger by automation, runtime resolution or qualification violates the profile.

grounding.quote:
each active layer should bind explicitly to local
typed assets or typed nodes, public graph-function carriers, the required
carried environment, proof or closure surfaces, and projection or query
surfaces.

constraints.statement: Each active layer should bind explicitly to local typed assets/nodes, public graph functions, required carried environment, proof/closure surfaces and projection/query surfaces; audits should distinguish structural law from local semantic bindings. Copying another Product's asset names without semantic need is accidental doctrine transfer, not method reuse. A prose capability without typed assets, graph functions and proof lanes is under-built.

conditions: Products are governed under ODD; mandatory resolution applies when a design/implementation move is not clearly covered.
exceptions: Product-local work may stay local when it changes no shared structural law.

grounding.quote:
An implementation or design move that the current profile does not
clearly cover must be evaluated against this profile

constraints.statement: Governed products should be audited. At minimum audit should ask capability/layer, binding assets/nodes, public constructive functions, proof/closure lane, projections that preserve ABG truth, attempted tenant-local replacement of continuation, and whether §11.5B proves ABG ownership of loops, invocation, supervision, retry/continuation, events and closure. Approved shared-pattern changes/clarifications must update the profile; grey work must not silently enter the line. Uncovered moves must resolve compliant, non-compliant or worth incorporation. Incorporation is not fully approved until profile update; non-compliance should be repriced, repaired or rejected, never normalised by repetition. Usage/drift ratifies no shared law; reusable structural law is ratified in the profile and local law in Product authority surfaces.

its name does not enrol it in
the project's collective evaluation frame set.

ABG Frame, attention frame, zoom frame and overlay frame remain ABG runtime contracts in WHAT/HOW; names do not enrol them as evaluation frames. A declared evaluation frame may inspect a runtime frame as exact subject/coordinate without identifying the two.
